root_cause.text: padata registered its CPU offline hotplug callback in the CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD teardown state even though padata_cpu_dead() could return an error, violating the CPU hotplug rule that callbacks before CPUHP_TEARDOWN_CPU must not fail.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “padata_cpu_dead() [is] the only sub-CPUHP_TEARDOWN_CPU callback that returns an error” and “Failure isn't allowed in hotplug states before CPUHP_TEARDOWN_CPU,” and the patch fixes this by removing CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD and registering padata_cpu_offline as the teardown callback in the ONLINE hotplug state where failure is allowed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the obsolete CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD CPU hotplug state from the cpuhp_state enum.
intent_record.what: The enum cpuhp_state definition was modified by removing the CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD enumerator from the sequence between CPUHP_AP_ARM_CACHE_B15_RAC_DEAD and CPUHP_AP_DTPM_CPU_DEAD.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates that CPU hotplug state identifier from the enum, so code can no longer refer to a distinct CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD dead-state slot and the numeric values of subsequent enum entries shift accordingly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unify padata CPU hotplug callback linkage and add an internal cpumask for validating configured masks during hotplug.
intent_record.what: The struct padata_instance definition was updated by replacing two hlist_node fields named cpu_online_node and cpu_dead_node with a single hlist_node field named cpuhp_node, and by adding a new cpumask_var_t field named validate_cpumask; the accompanying struct comment was updated to describe the unified CPU hotplug callback linkage and the new internal validation cpumask.
intent_record.how: At runtime this changes the instance state layout to support a single CPU hotplug registration hook instead of separate online and offline callback link nodes, and adds storage for an internal cpumask used to validate the user-provided cpumask during CPU hotplug events.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend padata_alloc_pd to accept an offlining CPU argument so CPU-offline context can be used during parallel_data allocation.
intent_record.what: The function signature of padata_alloc_pd was changed to add a second parameter, an int named offlining_cpu, and the declaration was reformatted across two lines; no other code changes are shown in this hunk.
intent_record.how: This change allows callers to pass CPU-offlining context into padata_alloc_pd at runtime, enabling subsequent implementation to make allocation or initialization decisions based on the specific CPU being offlined; by itself, this hunk only extends the interface.

intent_record.intent_summary: Exclude a CPU being offlined from newly allocated padata cpumasks so work is not scheduled to a CPU during hot-unplug transition.
intent_record.what: In padata_alloc_pd(), after intersecting pd->cpumask.pcpu and pd->cpumask.cbcpu with cpu_online_mask, a new conditional block was added that checks whether offlining_cpu is nonnegative and, if so, explicitly clears that CPU from both pd->cpumask.pcpu and pd->cpumask.cbcpu using __cpumask_clear_cpu().
intent_record.how: At runtime, when a CPU is in the process of being offlined, the newly allocated parallel_data cpumasks will no longer include that CPU even if it still appears online at that moment, preventing padata from assigning parallel or callback work to a CPU that is transitioning out of service.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the offlining CPU through padata_replace_one() so replacement parallel data is rebuilt correctly during CPU offline handling.
intent_record.what: The function padata_replace_one() was changed to take an additional int parameter named offlining_cpu, and its internal call to padata_alloc_pd(ps) was updated to pass that new argument as padata_alloc_pd(ps, offlining_cpu).
intent_record.how: At runtime, padata_replace_one() now propagates CPU offlining context to padata_alloc_pd(), allowing the replacement parallel_data structure to be allocated with awareness of which CPU is being taken offline instead of always using the generic allocation path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend padata_replace to accept the offlining CPU so replacement handling can account for CPU offlining context.
intent_record.what: The static function declaration and definition of padata_replace were changed to add a second parameter, an int named offlining_cpu, changing the signature from padata_replace(struct padata_instance *pinst) to padata_replace(struct padata_instance *pinst, int offlining_cpu).
intent_record.how: This change allows callers and the function implementation to receive and potentially use the CPU identifier associated with an offlining event, enabling padata_replace to make decisions based on which CPU is being taken offline. In the shown hunk alone, it changes the function interface but does not yet show the runtime logic that uses the new argument.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the offlining CPU into padata_replace_one() so padata replacement handles CPU offlining correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to padata_replace_one() inside padata_replace() was changed from taking only ps to taking ps and an additional offlining_cpu argument.
intent_record.how: At runtime, each replacement operation in the loop now receives the offlining_cpu context, enabling padata_replace_one() to make CPU-offlining-aware replacement decisions instead of operating without that information.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix padata cpumask validation during CPU hot-unplug by excluding the offlining CPU from the online mask check.
intent_record.what: The function padata_validate_cpumask() was changed to take an additional int parameter named offlining_cpu, copy cpu_online_mask into pinst->validate_cpumask, optionally clear offlining_cpu from that copied mask when offlining_cpu >= 0, and use the resulting mask in cpumask_intersects() instead of directly checking against cpu_online_mask; a comment was also added explaining why the offlining CPU is removed manually during validation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cpumask validation now treats a CPU currently being offlined as effectively already offline when deciding whether the supplied cpumask still contains any active CPUs. This prevents validation from incorrectly considering an instance valid solely because the soon-to-be-removed CPU is still present in cpu_online_mask during the hotplug callback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update cpumask validation calls to use the new three-argument interface with the default selector so CPU mask setup is validated correctly.
intent_record.what: The two calls to padata_validate_cpumask() in __padata_set_cpumasks() were updated to pass an additional third argument, changing both invocations from padata_validate_cpumask(pinst, <mask>) to padata_validate_cpumask(pinst, <mask>, -1).
intent_record.how: At runtime, cpumask validation in __padata_set_cpumasks() now uses the newer validation interface with a third parameter set to -1, which likely indicates no specific CPU exclusion or a default validation mode; this ensures the function call matches the updated validator semantics and preserves correct mask validation behavior when setting the parallelization and callback CPU masks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the default sentinel value to padata_replace during CPU mask updates so replacement logic executes with the correct updated interface and behavior.
intent_record.what: The call to padata_replace in __padata_set_cpumasks was modified from padata_replace(pinst) to padata_replace(pinst, -1) while keeping the surrounding conditional assignment logic unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the replacement operation to explicitly pass -1 as an additional argument, causing padata_replace to run with a specific sentinel/default parameter instead of relying on the previous no-argument form; this aligns the call with the updated function interface and ensures the replacement logic uses the intended default behavior when CPU masks are reset.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the local CPU hotplug add/remove wrapper helpers so their padata start/stop and replace handling can be managed elsewhere.
intent_record.what: Two static helper functions under CONFIG_HOTPLUG_CPU, __padata_add_cpu() and __padata_remove_cpu(), were deleted. The removed add helper called padata_replace(pinst), conditionally invoked __padata_start(pinst) when both cpumasks validated, and returned the replace result. The removed remove helper conditionally invoked __padata_stop(pinst) when either cpumask failed validation, then returned padata_replace(pinst).
intent_record.how: This change removes the local CPU hotplug add/remove wrapper logic that previously handled start/stop transitions around padata_replace(). As shown in this hunk, those helper entry points are no longer available, implying that CPU hotplug handling will no longer use these local wrappers and that the start/stop sequencing they performed must be handled elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix padata CPU hotplug handling by stopping on invalid offline transitions, rebuilding CPU state via padata_replace, and restarting only when the CPU masks are valid.
intent_record.what: The CPU hotplug callbacks were changed so that both functions now retrieve the padata instance from a single cpuhp_node field instead of separate cpu_online_node/cpu_dead_node fields, padata_cpu_dead was renamed to padata_cpu_offline, the online path replaced a direct __padata_add_cpu(pinst, cpu) call with padata_replace(pinst, -1) followed by conditional __padata_start(pinst) when both cpumasks validate, and the offline path replaced a direct __padata_remove_cpu(pinst, cpu) call with a pre-check that conditionally calls __padata_stop(pinst) when either cpumask would become invalid and then calls padata_replace(pinst, cpu).
intent_record.how: At runtime, CPU hotplug handling now rebuilds or replaces padata's CPU configuration through padata_replace instead of directly adding or removing one CPU, and it explicitly stops padata before offlining a CPU that would leave an invalid parallel or callback CPU mask, then restarts it on online only when both masks are valid again. This prevents padata from running with an unusable CPU mask during CPU hotplug transitions and enables safe recovery when CPUs come back online.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix padata instance teardown by unregistering the correct consolidated hotplug node and freeing validate_cpumask.
intent_record.what: In __padata_free(), the code removes two hotplug state instance removals for cpu_dead_node and cpu_online_node and replaces them with a single cpuhp_state_remove_instance_nocalls(hp_online, &pinst->cpuhp_node) call; it also adds free_cpumask_var(pinst->validate_cpumask) before destroying workqueues and freeing the instance.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes cleanup to unregister only the consolidated CPU hotplug instance node instead of two separate nodes, and it releases the validate_cpumask allocation during instance teardown, preventing stale hotplug registration state and a memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allocate validate_cpumask during padata instance creation and route allocation failures through proper cleanup paths.
intent_record.what: In padata_alloc(), the failure handling after allocating cpumask variables was changed: the inline block that freed pinst->cpumask.pcpu when alloc_cpumask_var(&pinst->cpumask.cbcpu, GFP_KERNEL) failed was removed and replaced with a goto to err_free_p_mask, and a new allocation call for pinst->validate_cpumask was added with failure jumping to err_free_cb_mask.
intent_record.how: At runtime, padata_alloc() now allocates an additional cpumask field, validate_cpumask, as part of instance setup, and uses centralized error paths to correctly unwind previously allocated masks if either cbcpu or validate_cpumask allocation fails, preventing leaks and ensuring the instance is fully initialized only when all required cpumasks are available.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix padata_alloc() failure cleanup to jump to the correct error-handling label when cpumask setup fails.
intent_record.what: The error path target after a failed call to padata_setup_cpumasks(pinst) in padata_alloc() was changed from goto err_free_masks; to goto err_free_v_mask;.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when padata_setup_cpumasks(pinst) fails, execution now jumps to a different cleanup label, which changes which resources are released during allocation failure handling and fixes the error unwinding sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix padata allocation by switching to a unified hotplug instance node and ensuring all allocated cpumasks are freed on error.
intent_record.what: The hotplug registration code was changed to call cpuhp_state_add_instance_nocalls_cpuslocked() only once with hp_online and pinst->cpuhp_node instead of twice with hp_online/pinst->cpu_online_node and CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD/pinst->cpu_dead_node. In the error path, the single err_free_masks label was replaced by three labels that separately free pinst->validate_cpumask, pinst->cpumask.cbcpu, and pinst->cpumask.pcpu in sequence.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the instance now uses a unified CPU hotplug node registration rather than separate online and dead nodes, and allocation failure cleanup now releases all allocated cpumask resources in the correct order, including validate_cpumask, preventing leaks during initialization failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update padata_alloc_shell() to pass the new default sentinel argument to padata_alloc_pd() so allocation uses the revised interface correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to padata_alloc_pd() in padata_alloc_shell() was changed from passing only ps to passing ps and an additional integer argument -1.
intent_record.how: At runtime, padata_alloc_shell() now invokes the updated padata_alloc_pd() interface with a sentinel value of -1, which likely requests default or unspecified behavior for the new parameter while preserving successful allocation flow under the CPU read lock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate padata CPU hotplug handling by using an offline callback on the online state and removing the separate dead-state registration and cleanup.
intent_record.what: The initialization code changes the cpuhp_setup_state_multi() call for the "padata:online" state to register padata_cpu_offline as the teardown callback instead of NULL, removes the separate cpuhp_setup_state_multi() registration for the "padata:dead" state with padata_cpu_dead, updates the kmalloc failure path to jump directly to remove_online_state instead of remove_dead_state, and deletes the remove_dead_state label and its cpuhp_remove_multi_state(CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD) cleanup.
intent_record.how: At runtime, padata now handles CPU hotplug teardown through the online state's offline callback rather than a separate dead-state hook. This simplifies hotplug state registration and ensures cleanup is tied to the registered online state, while also removing cleanup logic for a state that is no longer created. On allocation failure, only the remaining registered hotplug state is removed.

candidates.rationale: This registers padata's CPU offline callback in the CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD teardown state. The root cause is precisely that the offline callback was placed in a teardown state before CPUHP_TEARDOWN_CPU even though it could fail.

In padata_cpu_dead(), this propagates the return value from __padata_remove_cpu(), allowing the offline hotplug callback to fail. That violates CPU hotplug rules for callbacks registered before CPUHP_TEARDOWN_CPU.
This invokes the removal path whose result is returned by padata_cpu_dead(). Since __padata_remove_cpu() can fail, using it in the dead-state callback made that callback error-returning.
In __padata_remove_cpu(), this directly returns the result of padata_replace(), making CPU removal capable of failing. This is the underlying reason padata_cpu_dead() could return an error.

This shows the replacement operation used during CPU offline is explicitly error-returning. Because the offline callback path was built on this fallible function, registering it in CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD violated hotplug callback semantics.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the registration of padata's CPU offline callback in the CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD teardown state. The root cause is that this state is before CPUHP_TEARDOWN_CPU, where callbacks must not fail, yet the registered callback path could return an error.
In padata_cpu_dead(), this propagates an error from the CPU offline callback. Because the callback was registered in CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD, allowing it to fail violates CPU hotplug teardown rules.
This invokes the CPU removal path during the offline callback. Since that path can fail, it is part of the chain that made the callback registered in CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD error-returning.

This makes __padata_remove_cpu() directly return the result of padata_replace(), which can fail. That fallibility propagates up to padata_cpu_dead(), contributing to the invalid error-returning teardown callback.

bic_trace_step.reason: The root cause is registering padata's CPU offline callback in the CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD teardown state even though the callback can fail. In this commit version, that vulnerable construct is present. The code explicitly registers a dead/offline callback with `cpuhp_setup_state_multi(CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD, "padata:dead", NULL, padata_cpu_dead);` and also adds/removes instances for that state with `cpuhp_state_add_instance_nocalls_cpuslocked(CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD, &pinst->node);` and `cpuhp_state_remove_instance_nocalls(CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD, &pinst->node);`. The callback function is `static int padata_cpu_dead(unsigned int cpu, struct hlist_node *node)`, and its body returns `ret`, which comes from calling into per-instance CPU removal logic. Since it is an `int`-returning teardown callback and the function propagates an error return, it can fail. That matches the vulnerable condition described: using the CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD teardown state for a callback that may return an error. The fix for the reported vulnerability would require moving this callback to an earlier dedicated hotplug state before `CPUHP_TEARDOWN_CPU` so that the callback is no longer registered in `CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD`. That fix is not present here; instead, this commit newly introduces the `CPUHP_PADATA_DEAD` registration for `padata_cpu_dead`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the hotplug callback registration logic clearly enough to decide. The vulnerable root cause is registering an offline callback in the teardown/dead path where the callback may fail. In this commit, the old notifier-based callback is removed and replaced with explicit hotplug state-machine callbacks: `padata_cpu_online()` and `padata_cpu_prep_down()`. The registration is done in `padata_driver_init()` with `cpuhp_setup_state_multi(CPUHP_AP_ONLINE_DYN, "padata:online", padata_cpu_online, padata_cpu_prep_down);`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is present.
